messages:
Deploy Bot: ALERT: Canary rollout r-20260315-34 -> model-inference-service: increased error rate (502/504) and p95 latency spike (+18%) starting at 1792003448. Canary weight=10%
Alex Chen: ack. oncall here, watching. pinging @Maria Gomez for infra view.
Maria Gomez: looking. I can see a spike in 5xx from model-inference, traces show timeouts to model backend during tail requests. topology: canary pods running v34.
Jun Park: noticed similar from dashboard, tailing logs now. A few stacks show repeated KV cache misses that correlate with long RT.
Alex Chen: can we quickly reduce canary traffic? if it's 10% -> set to 0 while we investigate.
Maria Gomez: applying flag change to cut canary weight. command:
```
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/toggle \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ********' \n  -d '{"release":"r-20260315-34","weight":0}'
```
Maria Gomez: flag toggle submitted. Deploy Bot: Canary weight for r-20260315-34 set to 0. Confirming routing shift. :white_check_mark:
Deploy Bot: NOTE: rollback recommended? recent metrics show sustained 5xx > threshold.
Jun Park: I can trigger a quick rollback of the deployment to stable (rev 42). Will coordinate with Maria to avoid double actions.
Priya Patel: flagging potential customer impact: two high-traffic customers (acme-inc, dataflowhq) saw elevated errors in their dashboards, reported via support. I'm drafting a short note.
Alex Chen: go ahead Jun. Use `kubectl rollout undo` and watch healthchecks. Keep us updated every 2 min.
Jun Park: running rollback now:
```
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/model-inference-service --to-revision=42
kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/model-inference-service
```
Jun Park: rollback started. pods terminating and new ones coming up. I'm watching logs for 5xx tail.
DevOps Bot: ACTION: autoscaler temporarily increased node pool to accommodate restart surge (+2 nodes).
Maria Gomez: I'm draining canary nodes and checking KV cache priming after rollback. Early hist: p95 back to normal on one AZ, but still noisy in eu-west-1.
Alex Chen: quick customer impact assessment: approx 8-12% of total requests hit the bad canary window during 18:20-18:28 UTC; errors were transient but caused retries/timeouts for some dedicated customers. Product/CS notified.
Priya Patel: message sent to affected customers (templated): "We're aware of increased errors between 18:20-18:28 UTC caused by a recent rollout. We've rolled back and are monitoring. We'll follow up with root cause."
Jun Park: rollback complete on all clusters, healthchecks passing. I see no new 5xx for the last 60s.
Deploy Bot: Canary r-20260315-34 has been deactivated and rollout reversed. Monitoring baseline restored.
Alex Chen: good. switching to monitoring mode. I'm going to hand off to night on-call. Jun, you're up for the handoff — please keep an eye for at least 1h and escalate if errors reappear.
Jun Park: ack, taking handoff. Summary for night on-call:
- Event: bad rollout r-20260315-34 caused 5xx/latency spike.
- Mitigation: flag weight -> 0, rollback to rev 42, drain nodes, autoscaler bump.
- Customer impact: 8-12% of requests affected, CS notified.
- Actions for next hour: watch p95 and 5xx, ensure KV cache warms, confirm eu-west-1 stability.
Alex Chen: handing pager to Jun Park. handoff done. If anything flares, @oncall-pager (DevOps Bot) will page.
DevOps Bot: INCIDENT: All clear metric threshold cleared; continuing elevated-log-watch for 30m.
Priya Patel: logging ticket INC-2026-412 and adding customers contacted. Will schedule postmortem draft tomorrow.
Alex Chen: closing this Slack thread for live mitigation. Jun - please post any follow-ups here and file timeline in the incident board. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Jun Park: will do. posting timeline to incident board now.
Deploy Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: r-20260315-34 rollback successful. Monitoring for 30m (auto-checkpoints enabled).
